summary: Documented Australian direct-service, mobile-service and collision-repair pathways, with a verified Brisbane Service Centre. This is a support-access assessment; it does not measure fault rates or repair waiting times.
network: Book in the Tesla app. Mobile Service depends on location and repair type; some work requires a Service Centre. Mount Gravatt is an official Brisbane service location. Check travel distance and collision-repair arrangements.
warrantyNote: Coverage varies by delivery date, model and trim. Model 3/Y delivered from 1 January 2026 have a five-year/unlimited-kilometre basic warranty; do not apply that change automatically to a used 2023 car. Warranty work uses Tesla service.

summary: BYD documents Australia-wide warranty and service specialists and says its service, parts and warranty network is still expanding. The developing label reflects that published expansion stage, rather than an inferred reliability penalty.
network: Official locator distinguishes experience centres from service centres. Confirm the nearest workshop supports your exact EV or DM-i model, and ask about parts and booking lead times; a sales location is not automatically a service workshop.
warrantyNote: Published Australian vehicle warranty is six years/150,000km and traction battery warranty eight years/160,000km, whichever occurs first. Component exclusions and the original vehicle warranty document still govern a used purchase.

summary: An authorised dealer network provides Australian servicing, parts and warranty work. This supports a mature service-access classification, without claiming that a Kia will have fewer faults.
network: Kia’s official locator lists sales plus service-and-parts contacts. Kia says warranty and service can be obtained at any authorised Kia dealer; verify the local workshop handles the relevant EV or hybrid.
warrantyNote: Kia advertises seven-year transferable vehicle warranty support. EV, battery, usage and component limits need the applicable model terms; record the remaining original cover rather than restarting seven years for a used car.

summary: Hyundai documents a national dealer network serving metropolitan and rural communities, with technician training and authorised service booking. Network presence is evidence of support access, not measured long-term vehicle reliability.
network: Use the official dealer/service locator and confirm Ioniq-specific EV capability. Hyundai distinguishes electrified-model locations and its authorised network provides genuine servicing and warranty support.
warrantyNote: Standard private passenger cover is five years/unlimited km. Eligible vehicles first registered from 1 June 2025 can reach seven years when all scheduled services meet authorised-dealer conditions. EV/hybrid drive batteries have separate eight-year/160,000km terms.

summary: Zeekr’s Australian market entry dates to 2024 and support is organised through authorised dealer partners. The developing label reflects its shorter local history; no failure-rate or parts-delay conclusion has been inferred.
network: The official Australian service page and dealer locator identify the authorised-partner channel. Confirm the nearest actual service location, model capability, parts supply and collision repair before choosing a car. Do not assume related-brand workshops are authorised.
warrantyNote: The current Australian policy linked by Zeekr states five years/unlimited km for private vehicles and eight years/160,000km for the high-voltage battery, subject to servicing and other terms. Promotional or model-specific cover may differ; verify the supplied policy for the VIN.

summary: Mitsubishi documents Australian authorised-dealer servicing, genuine parts and a service-linked extended-warranty program. These are support arrangements rather than evidence of a particular Outlander’s mechanical condition.
network: The Australian genuine-service program uses authorised dealers with factory repair information and genuine parts. Confirm the workshop’s Outlander PHEV capability and the actual vehicle’s service history.
warrantyNote: Standard cover is five years/100,000km; eligible vehicles can have up to ten years/200,000km when scheduled services satisfy Mitsubishi dealer conditions. A used vehicle needs evidence of eligibility and service compliance; battery coverage is separate.

summary: Nissan documents an Australian authorised dealer/service network, trained technicians, genuine parts and owner support. This is a support-access proxy and does not predict e-POWER fault frequency.
network: Use the official dealer locator and ask whether the service workshop supports X-Trail e-POWER. Servicing, parts, roadside assistance and owner support are available through Nissan’s Australian ownership program.
warrantyNote: Nissan MORE offers eligible vehicles service-activated cover up to ten years/300,000km. The underlying standard protection remains five years/unlimited km plus qualifying activated extensions. Verify registration-date eligibility and the used vehicle’s service record.

summary: Toyota documents Australian dealer support for servicing, parts and warranty claims. Its support classification reflects those established channels, not a claim that every RAV4 or Kluger is trouble-free.
network: The official Australian locator provides dealer/service contacts. Check the closest workshop and appointments for your actual hybrid, and obtain its service and battery-health history.
warrantyNote: Private new vehicles purchased from 1 January 2019 have five-year/unlimited-kilometre cover, with the unexpired balance remaining with a used car. Engine/driveline and traction-battery extensions require the applicable servicing and health-check conditions.
